text:
Detroit and Edmonton both arrive after a loss two days ago. The Red Wings fell 4-1 at Calgary despite 65% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality), and they are still 3-1-1 in their last five without Mason Appleton and Marco Kasper. The Oilers' three-game winning streak ended in a 7-2 home loss to Toronto, and they are missing Mattias Ekholm. Ryan Shea has moved in beside Evan Bouchard, and Shakir Mukhamadullin is up to 17:28 a night from 12:05.

The teams look close on chances. Over the season, DET has 53% of the expected goals at five on five and EDM 49%, but the Oilers' results are running ahead of their chances, while the Red Wings are better than their record. Special teams give us a matchup to watch: EDM's power play creates 0.91 expected goals a game against a DET penalty kill allowing 0.78, and Detroit takes 4.5 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Michal Postava (one game, .875) and Tristan Jarry (-6.58 goals saved above expected, which compares his saves with what the shots should have produced, after -4.19 last season) both enter shaky.

Connor McDavid is on an 11-game point streak with 31 points in 10 games, and we give him a 92% chance at a point. Leon Draisaitl has scored in six straight and is our pick at 44% to score; as Oilersnation posted, he was named the NHL's first star of the week. For Detroit, Lucas Raymond, drafted fourth overall in 2020, had three points Thursday against Vancouver, and Alex DeBrincat leads the Wings at 38% to score.
